result.instructions:
This server drives the Unity Editor. Core conventions:

- Non-image tool results are JSON envelopes. Success is `{ "success": true, "message": "...", ... }` with an optional payload under `data`; failure is `{ "success": false, "code": "...", ... }`. Branch on `code`, never on human-readable text. Inline screenshots are returned as MCP image content.
- Edit scenes, prefabs, and ScriptableObjects ONLY through these tools / Unity Editor APIs. Never hand-edit .unity/.prefab/.asset files as text while the Editor is open - it overwrites your changes from its in-memory copy.
- To change serialized fields on one prefab component, prefer `set_prefab_property` / `set_prefab_properties`. They avoid Prefab Mode, synchronously reimport the asset, and return persisted readback. Use `open_prefab_stage` only for structural edits; a stage save serializes the full in-memory prefab graph, so review its warning and verify the result afterward.
- Inspect an object before mutating a user-named target; treat user-supplied names as hints, not paths. Carry the returned `instanceId` into follow-up calls (`find_method=by_id`) instead of re-resolving by name.
- After editing scripts outside Unity, call `request_recompile`, `wait_for_compilation`, then `get_compilation_errors`. `request_recompile` is rejected in Play Mode - call `exit_play_mode` first. After `enter_play_mode`, poll `get_reload_recovery_status` until ready before the next call (the HTTP server briefly drops during domain reload).
- `get_console_logs` accepts `group_duplicates=true` to collapse spammy repeated logs and `filter_text` to narrow them.
- Large screenshot results automatically fall back to a project-local file. Prefer `save_to_file` when the client can read local files, and use explicit width/height when only a small inline preview is needed.
- Save only the assets you intentionally changed, then read them back to confirm the exact values.

tools.name: execute_code
tools.description:
[primary] [core] Primary high-flexibility execution tool. Compiles a C# snippet with Unity's Roslyn csc first while preserving the in-memory compilation/execution flow, then runs the compiled assembly on the editor thread. Two templates are supported:
  1) Recommended: implement IFunplayCommand on a class — receives an ExecutionContext (ctx) with RegisterObjectCreation/RegisterObjectModification/DestroyObject (auto-Undo + tracked) and Log/LogWarning/LogError (returned in the response).
  2) Legacy: any class with `public static string Run()` — return value becomes the response message.
Before compiling, the editor's AssetDatabase is refreshed and pending compilation is awaited, so external file edits are picked up automatically without a separate request_recompile (pass skip_refresh=true to bypass this for read-only snippets or a live Play Mode session you must not disturb). When a full-class snippet implements IFunplayCommand, the required Funplay.Editor.Tools.Scripting using is added automatically if omitted. The snippet is compiled into a SEPARATE assembly, so funplay package internal types (e.g. ToolRegistry) cannot be referenced directly from the snippet -- reach them via reflection. safety_checks blocks a small set of obviously dangerous patterns (File.Delete, Process.Start, while(true), Environment.Exit, AssetDatabase.DeleteAsset, etc) and, when strict filesystem safety is enabled, broad System.IO writes plus obvious absolute/system/traversal paths. This is a defensive layer, not a full sandbox. If omitted, the MCP Settings window's default safety-check setting is used (enabled by default); explicitly passing true or false overrides that default. Project namespaces are not auto-injected by default; add `using` directives in the snippet, or enable the ScriptAssemblies-based convenience toggle in the MCP Settings window. If a compile fails with CS0104 (a type name ambiguous between two imported namespaces, e.g. System.Random vs UnityEngine.Random) or CS0433 (a type provided by multiple loaded assemblies) the error carries a structured `ambiguous` list; for CS0104 pass preferred_namespaces (comma-separated) to auto-insert a using-alias binding the name to that namespace and recompile once. CS0433 (same fully-qualified type in two assemblies) can't be fixed by an alias — use extern alias / drop a reference / reflection. Every invocation is appended to a session-scoped history (see get_execute_code_history / replay_execute_code).

code.description: C# code to execute. See description for IFunplayCommand vs legacy Run() templates.

safety_checks.description: If true, reject the call before compile when the code contains obviously dangerous patterns. If omitted, uses the MCP Settings window default.

skip_refresh.description: If true, skip the pre-compile AssetDatabase.Refresh + wait-for-ready. Use only when the editor is already up to date -- e.g. a read-only inspection snippet, or during a live Play Mode session you must not disturb. The default refresh can trigger an import/domain reload (from your own OR another actor's pending changes in a shared editor) that wipes Play Mode runtime state. When skipped, external file edits made since the last compile are NOT picked up.

preferred_namespaces.description: Optional comma-separated namespaces used to auto-resolve CS0104 ambiguity: when an unqualified type name is ambiguous between two imported namespaces, a using-alias binding that name to the candidate in the listed (winning) namespace is inserted and the snippet is recompiled once. Does NOT fix CS0433 (same fully-qualified type in two assemblies). If it stays ambiguous, a structured COMPILATION_FAILED error with an `ambiguous` array is returned.

tools.description: [core] Get information about every loaded scene (the active scene plus any additively loaded ones), including path, dirty state, and a shallow root-object hierarchy per scene.

tools.description: [core] Get the current Hierarchy selection: instance ids, names, and paths.

tools.name: get_time_scale
tools.description: [core] Get the current time scale and time information

tools.description: [core] List components on a GameObject. Each entry includes its instanceId so subsequent set_component_property calls can disambiguate when a GameObject has multiple components of the same type.

target.description: GameObject identifier (instance id, name, path, tag…)

tools.name: raycast_at_point
tools.description: [core] Diagnose what UI (or physics) elements a click/tap at a screen point would hit, using the live EventSystem's RaycastAll. x.description: X coordinate of the point to test.

y.description: Y coordinate of the point to test.

normalized.description: Interpret x/y as normalized 0-1 viewport coordinates instead of pixels.

origin.description: Coordinate origin: 'bottom_left' (Unity screen space, default) or 'top_left' (screenshot/image space).

max_results.description: Maximum number of hits to include in the result. Default 20.

tools.name: request_recompile
tools.description: [core] IMPORTANT: This should be the AI's default next step immediately after editing project files outside the Unity Editor. Treat this as required after any external code or asset change. Call it after modifying .cs, .asmdef, .shader, prefabs, scenes, ScriptableObjects, or other Assets files, and before running tests, entering Play Mode, executing follow-up tools, or assuming Unity has imported the latest state. timeout_seconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait for compilation

tools.name: set_component_properties
tools.description: [core] Set multiple properties on a component in one call. Pass `properties` as a JSON object: {"mass": 5, "isKinematic": true, "material": {"fileID": 12345}}. Returns per-field success so partial failures are diagnosable, plus the post-write serialized values of the fields that applied ('applied'). Pass `targets` (comma-separated identifiers, or a find spec resolving to at most 100 objects) with a `component` type name to apply the SAME properties to many objects (returns per-target results).

target.description: GameObject identifier (omit if using component_instance_id or targets)

component.description: Component type name (omit if using component_instance_id)

targets.description: Comma-separated identifiers, or a find spec resolving to at most 100 objects (batch; requires `component`)

tools.name: set_component_property
tools.description: [core] Set a single property or field on a component. Use simple JSON for value (e.g. '5', 'true', '"text"', '[1,2,3]'). For Object references pass {"fileID": <instanceId>} or {"assetPath": "Assets/..."}. The success response echoes the post-write serialized value ('newValue'). Pass `targets` (comma-separated identifiers, or a find spec resolving to at most 100 objects) with a `component` type name to apply the SAME field to many objects (returns per-target results).

target.description: GameObject identifier (omit if using component_instance_id or targets)

component.description: Component type name (omit if using component_instance_id)

targets.description: Comma-separated identifiers, or a find spec resolving to at most 100 objects (batch; requires `component`)

tools.name: set_prefab_properties
tools.description: [core] Set multiple serialized fields on one component in a prefab asset without opening Prefab Mode. Path validation, ambiguity handling, save, synchronous reimport, and persisted readback match set_prefab_property. Pass properties as a JSON object. Fields are applied independently and the response reports partial failures; if every field fails, the tool returns an error and does not save the asset.

component.description: Component type name

game_object_path.description: Exact '/'-separated child path relative to the prefab root (empty or '/' = root)

game_object_index.description: Zero-based match index when duplicate hierarchy paths exist; omit to reject ambiguity

component_index.description: Zero-based match index when the target has duplicate components of this type; omit to reject ambiguity

tools.name: set_prefab_property
tools.description: [core] Set one serialized field on a component in a prefab asset without opening Prefab Mode. The prefab path must be a normalized Assets/**/*.prefab path. Exact hierarchy and component matches are required; pass game_object_index or component_index only after an ambiguity response identifies duplicates. This avoids live Prefab Stage layout/TMP/Spine recomputation, but Unity serialization callbacks can still run. The asset is saved with PrefabUtility, synchronously reimported, and the persisted value is read back. Only serialized fields are accepted; public-member reflection fallback is intentionally disabled. For structural edits such as adding, removing, or reparenting objects, use Prefab Mode.

component.description: Component type name (e.g. 'TextMeshProUGUI', 'UnityEngine.UI.Image')

game_object_path.description: Exact '/'-separated child path relative to the prefab root (empty or '/' = root)

game_object_index.description: Zero-based match index when duplicate hierarchy paths exist; omit to reject ambiguity

component_index.description: Zero-based match index when the target has duplicate components of this type; omit to reject ambiguity

tools.name: set_selection
tools.description: [core] Replace the current selection. Pass either a comma-separated list of instance ids, names, or paths. Use find_method to control how each token is resolved (by_id, by_name, by_path).

targets.description: Comma-separated instance ids, names, or paths

find_method.description: How to resolve each token (by_id, by_name, by_path, by_id_or_name_or_path)

tools.name: simulate_key_combo
tools.description: [core] Simulate multiple keys held simultaneously in Play Mode, for example W plus LeftShift.

keys.description: Comma-separated key names, for example 'W,LeftShift' or 'A,Space'

duration.description: Duration in seconds to hold the combo

tools.name: simulate_key_press
tools.description: [core] Simulate keyboard input in Play Mode. Queues key events that the Unity Input System will process. Supports key names like W, A, S, D, Space, LeftShift, E, Q, and number keys.

key.description: Key name, for example W, Space, LeftShift, E, or 1

duration.description: Duration in seconds to hold the key. Use 0 for a tap.

action.description: Action type: press, release, or tap

tools.name: simulate_mouse_click
tools.description: [core] Simulate a mouse click at a screen position in Play Mode. Coordinates are in screen pixels with 0,0 at the bottom-left. Works without the Input System by dispatching UI and physics events. Returns a structured result reporting whether a target was actually hit, by which strategy, and the object that was clicked (or null when nothing was hit).

x.description: Screen X coordinate in pixels

y.description: Screen Y coordinate in pixels

button.description: Mouse button: left, right, or middle

tools.name: simulate_mouse_drag
tools.description: [core] Simulate a mouse drag from one screen position to another in Play Mode using the Unity Input System.

duration.description: Duration of the drag in seconds

button.description: Mouse button: left, right, or middle

tools.name: wait_for_compilation
tools.description: [core] Force Unity to refresh and wait until script compilation is complete without blocking the editor thread. Use this after editing scripts to ensure the latest code is active before entering Play Mode. Returns compilation errors if any, or a success message.

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait for compilation

result.instructions:
This server drives the Unity Editor. Core conventions:

- Non-image tool results are JSON envelopes. Success is `{ "success": true, "message": "...", ... }` with an optional payload under `data`; failure is `{ "success": false, "code": "...", ... }`. Branch on `code`, never on human-readable text. Inline screenshots are returned as MCP image content.
- Edit scenes, prefabs, and ScriptableObjects ONLY through these tools / Unity Editor APIs. Never hand-edit .unity/.prefab/.asset files as text while the Editor is open - it overwrites your changes from its in-memory copy.
- To change serialized fields on one prefab component, prefer `set_prefab_property` / `set_prefab_properties`. They avoid Prefab Mode, synchronously reimport the asset, and return persisted readback. Use `open_prefab_stage` only for structural edits; a stage save serializes the full in-memory prefab graph, so review its warning and verify the result afterward.
- Inspect an object before mutating a user-named target; treat user-supplied names as hints, not paths. Carry the returned `instanceId` into follow-up calls (`find_method=by_id`) instead of re-resolving by name.
- After editing scripts outside Unity, call `request_recompile`, `wait_for_compilation`, then `get_compilation_errors`. `request_recompile` is rejected in Play Mode - call `exit_play_mode` first. After `enter_play_mode`, poll `get_reload_recovery_status` until ready before the next call (the HTTP server briefly drops during domain reload).
- `get_console_logs` accepts `group_duplicates=true` to collapse spammy repeated logs and `filter_text` to narrow them.
- Large screenshot results automatically fall back to a project-local file. Prefer `save_to_file` when the client can read local files, and use explicit width/height when only a small inline preview is needed.
- Save only the assets you intentionally changed, then read them back to confirm the exact values.

tools.name: execute_code
tools.description:
[primary] [core] Primary high-flexibility execution tool. Compiles a C# snippet with Unity's Roslyn csc first while preserving the in-memory compilation/execution flow, then runs the compiled assembly on the editor thread. Two templates are supported:
  1) Recommended: implement IFunplayCommand on a class — receives an ExecutionContext (ctx) with RegisterObjectCreation/RegisterObjectModification/DestroyObject (auto-Undo + tracked) and Log/LogWarning/LogError (returned in the response).
  2) Legacy: any class with `public static string Run()` — return value becomes the response message.
Before compiling, the editor's AssetDatabase is refreshed and pending compilation is awaited, so external file edits are picked up automatically without a separate request_recompile (pass skip_refresh=true to bypass this for read-only snippets or a live Play Mode session you must not disturb). When a full-class snippet implements IFunplayCommand, the required Funplay.Editor.Tools.Scripting using is added automatically if omitted. The snippet is compiled into a SEPARATE assembly, so funplay package internal types (e.g. ToolRegistry) cannot be referenced directly from the snippet -- reach them via reflection. safety_checks blocks a small set of obviously dangerous patterns (File.Delete, Process.Start, while(true), Environment.Exit, AssetDatabase.DeleteAsset, etc) and, when strict filesystem safety is enabled, broad System.IO writes plus obvious absolute/system/traversal paths. This is a defensive layer, not a full sandbox. If omitted, the MCP Settings window's default safety-check setting is used (enabled by default); explicitly passing true or false overrides that default. Project namespaces are not auto-injected by default; add `using` directives in the snippet, or enable the ScriptAssemblies-based convenience toggle in the MCP Settings window. If a compile fails with CS0104 (a type name ambiguous between two imported namespaces, e.g. System.Random vs UnityEngine.Random) or CS0433 (a type provided by multiple loaded assemblies) the error carries a structured `ambiguous` list; for CS0104 pass preferred_namespaces (comma-separated) to auto-insert a using-alias binding the name to that namespace and recompile once. CS0433 (same fully-qualified type in two assemblies) can't be fixed by an alias — use extern alias / drop a reference / reflection. Every invocation is appended to a session-scoped history (see get_execute_code_history / replay_execute_code).

code.description: C# code to execute. See description for IFunplayCommand vs legacy Run() templates.

safety_checks.description: If true, reject the call before compile when the code contains obviously dangerous patterns. If omitted, uses the MCP Settings window default.

skip_refresh.description: If true, skip the pre-compile AssetDatabase.Refresh + wait-for-ready. Use only when the editor is already up to date -- e.g. a read-only inspection snippet, or during a live Play Mode session you must not disturb. The default refresh can trigger an import/domain reload (from your own OR another actor's pending changes in a shared editor) that wipes Play Mode runtime state. When skipped, external file edits made since the last compile are NOT picked up.

preferred_namespaces.description: Optional comma-separated namespaces used to auto-resolve CS0104 ambiguity: when an unqualified type name is ambiguous between two imported namespaces, a using-alias binding that name to the candidate in the listed (winning) namespace is inserted and the snippet is recompiled once. Does NOT fix CS0433 (same fully-qualified type in two assemblies). If it stays ambiguous, a structured COMPILATION_FAILED error with an `ambiguous` array is returned.

When a full-class snippet implements IFunplayCommand, the required Funplay.Editor.Tools.Scripting using is added automatically if omitted. Captures directly from the window's render surface via the editor's internal GUIView, so the window does not need to be unoccluded on screen (it does need to be open). Returns a base64-encoded PNG image, or a saved file path when save_to_file=true.

window.description: Window title (e.g. 'Inspector', 'MCP Server') or window type name (e.g. 'ConsoleWindow'). Case-insensitive. Exact title match wins, then title contains, then type name.

width.description: Width of the screenshot in pixels. 0 keeps the window's native size.

height.description: Height of the screenshot in pixels. 0 keeps the window's native size.

save_to_file.description: Save the PNG to disk and return its file path instead of base64 image data. Use for high-resolution captures whose base64 payload would be too large for the transport.

output_path.description: Optional output .png path under the Unity project root (absolute, or relative to the project root). Default: Library/FunplayMcp/Screenshots/<name>-<timestamp>.png. Only used when save_to_file=true.

focus.description: Focus the window before capturing (brings its tab to the front of its dock area). Default true.

tools.name: capture_game_view

width.description: Width of the screenshot in pixels

height.description: Height of the screenshot in pixels

output_path.description: Optional output .png path under the Unity project root (absolute, or relative to the project root). Default: Library/FunplayMcp/Screenshots/<name>-<timestamp>.png. Only used when save_to_file=true.

tools.name: raycast_at_point
tools.description: [core] Diagnose what UI (or physics) elements a click/tap at a screen point would hit, using the live EventSystem's RaycastAll. Requires a live EventSystem (Play Mode).

y.description: Y coordinate of the point to test.

normalized.description: Interpret x/y as normalized 0-1 viewport coordinates instead of pixels.

origin.description: Coordinate origin: 'bottom_left' (Unity screen space, default) or 'top_left' (screenshot/image space).

max_results.description: Maximum number of hits to include in the result. Default 20.

Pass `targets` (comma-separated identifiers, or a find spec resolving to at most 100 objects) with a `component` type name to apply the SAME properties to many objects (returns per-target results).

component.description: Component type name (omit if using component_instance_id)

targets.description: Comma-separated identifiers, or a find spec resolving to at most 100 objects (batch; requires `component`)

tools.name: set_component_property

target.description: GameObject identifier (omit if using component_instance_id or targets)

tools.name: set_prefab_property

result.instructions:
This server drives the Unity Editor. Core conventions:

- Non-image tool results are JSON envelopes. Success is `{ "success": true, "message": "...", ... }` with an optional payload under `data`; failure is `{ "success": false, "code": "...", ... }`. Branch on `code`, never on human-readable text. Inline screenshots are returned as MCP image content.
- Edit scenes, prefabs, and ScriptableObjects ONLY through these tools / Unity Editor APIs. Never hand-edit .unity/.prefab/.asset files as text while the Editor is open - it overwrites your changes from its in-memory copy.
- To change serialized fields on one prefab component, prefer `set_prefab_property` / `set_prefab_properties`. They avoid Prefab Mode, synchronously reimport the asset, and return persisted readback. Use `open_prefab_stage` only for structural edits; a stage save serializes the full in-memory prefab graph, so review its warning and verify the result afterward.
- Inspect an object before mutating a user-named target; treat user-supplied names as hints, not paths. Carry the returned `instanceId` into follow-up calls (`find_method=by_id`) instead of re-resolving by name.
- After editing scripts outside Unity, call `request_recompile`, `wait_for_compilation`, then `get_compilation_errors`. `request_recompile` is rejected in Play Mode - call `exit_play_mode` first. After `enter_play_mode`, poll `get_reload_recovery_status` until ready before the next call (the HTTP server briefly drops during domain reload).
- `get_console_logs` accepts `group_duplicates=true` to collapse spammy repeated logs and `filter_text` to narrow them.
- Large screenshot results automatically fall back to a project-local file. Prefer `save_to_file` when the client can read local files, and use explicit width/height when only a small inline preview is needed.
- Save only the assets you intentionally changed, then read them back to confirm the exact values.

tools.name: execute_code
tools.description:
[primary] [core] Primary high-flexibility execution tool. Compiles a C# snippet with Unity's Roslyn csc first while preserving the in-memory compilation/execution flow, then runs the compiled assembly on the editor thread. Two templates are supported:
  1) Recommended: implement IFunplayCommand on a class — receives an ExecutionContext (ctx) with RegisterObjectCreation/RegisterObjectModification/DestroyObject (auto-Undo + tracked) and Log/LogWarning/LogError (returned in the response).
  2) Legacy: any class with `public static string Run()` — return value becomes the response message.
Before compiling, the editor's AssetDatabase is refreshed and pending compilation is awaited, so external file edits are picked up automatically without a separate request_recompile (pass skip_refresh=true to bypass this for read-only snippets or a live Play Mode session you must not disturb). When a full-class snippet implements IFunplayCommand, the required Funplay.Editor.Tools.Scripting using is added automatically if omitted. The snippet is compiled into a SEPARATE assembly, so funplay package internal types (e.g. ToolRegistry) cannot be referenced directly from the snippet -- reach them via reflection. safety_checks blocks a small set of obviously dangerous patterns (File.Delete, Process.Start, while(true), Environment.Exit, AssetDatabase.DeleteAsset, etc) and, when strict filesystem safety is enabled, broad System.IO writes plus obvious absolute/system/traversal paths. This is a defensive layer, not a full sandbox. If omitted, the MCP Settings window's default safety-check setting is used (enabled by default); explicitly passing true or false overrides that default. Project namespaces are not auto-injected by default; add `using` directives in the snippet, or enable the ScriptAssemblies-based convenience toggle in the MCP Settings window. If a compile fails with CS0104 (a type name ambiguous between two imported namespaces, e.g. System.Random vs UnityEngine.Random) or CS0433 (a type provided by multiple loaded assemblies) the error carries a structured `ambiguous` list; for CS0104 pass preferred_namespaces (comma-separated) to auto-insert a using-alias binding the name to that namespace and recompile once. CS0433 (same fully-qualified type in two assemblies) can't be fixed by an alias — use extern alias / drop a reference / reflection. Every invocation is appended to a session-scoped history (see get_execute_code_history / replay_execute_code).

code.description: C# code to execute. See description for IFunplayCommand vs legacy Run() templates.

safety_checks.description: If true, reject the call before compile when the code contains obviously dangerous patterns. If omitted, uses the MCP Settings window default.

skip_refresh.description: If true, skip the pre-compile AssetDatabase.Refresh + wait-for-ready. Use only when the editor is already up to date -- e.g. a read-only inspection snippet, or during a live Play Mode session you must not disturb. The default refresh can trigger an import/domain reload (from your own OR another actor's pending changes in a shared editor) that wipes Play Mode runtime state. When skipped, external file edits made since the last compile are NOT picked up.

preferred_namespaces.description: Optional comma-separated namespaces used to auto-resolve CS0104 ambiguity: when an unqualified type name is ambiguous between two imported namespaces, a using-alias binding that name to the candidate in the listed (winning) namespace is inserted and the snippet is recompiled once. Does NOT fix CS0433 (same fully-qualified type in two assemblies). If it stays ambiguous, a structured COMPILATION_FAILED error with an `ambiguous` array is returned.

tools.name: execute_code
tools.description:
[primary] [core] Primary high-flexibility execution tool. Compiles a C# snippet with Unity's Roslyn csc first while preserving the in-memory compilation/execution flow, then runs the compiled assembly on the editor thread. Two templates are supported:
  1) Recommended: implement IFunplayCommand on a class — receives an ExecutionContext (ctx) with RegisterObjectCreation/RegisterObjectModification/DestroyObject (auto-Undo + tracked) and Log/LogWarning/LogError (returned in the response).
  2) Legacy: any class with `public static string Run()` — return value becomes the response message.
Before compiling, the editor's AssetDatabase is refreshed and pending compilation is awaited, so external file edits are picked up automatically without a separate request_recompile (pass skip_refresh=true to bypass this for read-only snippets or a live Play Mode session you must not disturb). When a full-class snippet implements IFunplayCommand, the required Funplay.Editor.Tools.Scripting using is added automatically if omitted. The snippet is compiled into a SEPARATE assembly, so funplay package internal types (e.g. ToolRegistry) cannot be referenced directly from the snippet -- reach them via reflection. safety_checks blocks a small set of obviously dangerous patterns (File.Delete, Process.Start, while(true), Environment.Exit, AssetDatabase.DeleteAsset, etc) and, when strict filesystem safety is enabled, broad System.IO writes plus obvious absolute/system/traversal paths. This is a defensive layer, not a full sandbox. If omitted, the MCP Settings window's default safety-check setting is used (enabled by default); explicitly passing true or false overrides that default. Project namespaces are not auto-injected by default; add `using` directives in the snippet, or enable the ScriptAssemblies-based convenience toggle in the MCP Settings window. If a compile fails with CS0104 (a type name ambiguous between two imported namespaces, e.g. System.Random vs UnityEngine.Random) or CS0433 (a type provided by multiple loaded assemblies) the error carries a structured `ambiguous` list; for CS0104 pass preferred_namespaces (comma-separated) to auto-insert a using-alias binding the name to that namespace and recompile once. CS0433 (same fully-qualified type in two assemblies) can't be fixed by an alias — use extern alias / drop a reference / reflection. Every invocation is appended to a session-scoped history (see get_execute_code_history / replay_execute_code).

safety_checks.description: If true, reject the call before compile when the code contains obviously dangerous patterns. If omitted, uses the MCP Settings window default.

Use only when the editor is already up to date -- e.g. a read-only inspection snippet, or during a live Play Mode session you must not disturb. The default refresh can trigger an import/domain reload (from your own OR another actor's pending changes in a shared editor) that wipes Play Mode runtime state.   1) Recommended: implement IFunplayCommand on a class — receives an ExecutionContext (ctx) with RegisterObjectCreation/RegisterObjectModification/DestroyObject (auto-Undo + tracked) and Log/LogWarning/LogError (returned in the response).
  2) Legacy: any class with `public static string Run()` — return value becomes the response message.
Before compiling, the editor's AssetDatabase is refreshed and pending compilation is awaited, so external file edits are picked up automatically without a separate request_recompile (pass skip_refresh=true to bypass this for read-only snippets or a live Play Mode session you must not disturb). When a full-class snippet implements IFunplayCommand, the required Funplay.Editor.Tools.Scripting using is added automatically if omitted. The snippet is compiled into a SEPARATE assembly, so funplay package internal types (e.g. ToolRegistry) cannot be referenced directly from the snippet -- reach them via reflection. safety_checks blocks a small set of obviously dangerous patterns (File.Delete, Process.Start, while(true), Environment.Exit, AssetDatabase.DeleteAsset, etc) and, when strict filesystem safety is enabled, broad System.IO writes plus obvious absolute/system/traversal paths. This is a defensive layer, not a full sandbox. If omitted, the MCP Settings window's default safety-check setting is used (enabled by default); explicitly passing true or false overrides that default. Project namespaces are not auto-injected by default; add `using` directives in the snippet, or enable the ScriptAssemblies-based convenience toggle in the MCP Settings window. If a compile fails with CS0104 (a type name ambiguous between two imported namespaces, e.g. System.Random vs UnityEngine.Random) or CS0433 (a type provided by multiple loaded assemblies) the error carries a structured `ambiguous` list; for CS0104 pass preferred_namespaces (comma-separated) to auto-insert a using-alias binding the name to that namespace and recompile once. CS0433 (same fully-qualified type in two assemblies) can't be fixed by an alias — use extern alias / drop a reference / reflection. Every invocation is appended to a session-scoped history (see get_execute_code_history / replay_execute_code).

code.description: C# code to execute. See description for IFunplayCommand vs legacy Run() templates.

safety_checks.description: If true, reject the call before compile when the code contains obviously dangerous patterns. If omitted, uses the MCP Settings window default.

skip_refresh.description: If true, skip the pre-compile AssetDatabase.Refresh + wait-for-ready. Use only when the editor is already up to date -- e.g. a read-only inspection snippet, or during a live Play Mode session you must not disturb. The default refresh can trigger an import/domain reload (from your own OR another actor's pending changes in a shared editor) that wipes Play Mode runtime state. When skipped, external file edits made since the last compile are NOT picked up.

preferred_namespaces.description: Optional comma-separated namespaces used to auto-resolve CS0104 ambiguity: when an unqualified type name is ambiguous between two imported namespaces, a using-alias binding that name to the candidate in the listed (winning) namespace is inserted and the snippet is recompiled once. Does NOT fix CS0433 (same fully-qualified type in two assemblies). If it stays ambiguous, a structured COMPILATION_FAILED error with an `ambiguous` array is returned.

result.instructions:
This server drives the Unity Editor. Core conventions:

- Non-image tool results are JSON envelopes. Success is `{ "success": true, "message": "...", ... }` with an optional payload under `data`; failure is `{ "success": false, "code": "...", ... }`. Branch on `code`, never on human-readable text. Inline screenshots are returned as MCP image content.
- Edit scenes, prefabs, and ScriptableObjects ONLY through these tools / Unity Editor APIs. Never hand-edit .unity/.prefab/.asset files as text while the Editor is open - it overwrites your changes from its in-memory copy.
- To change serialized fields on one prefab component, prefer `set_prefab_property` / `set_prefab_properties`. They avoid Prefab Mode, synchronously reimport the asset, and return persisted readback. Use `open_prefab_stage` only for structural edits; a stage save serializes the full in-memory prefab graph, so review its warning and verify the result afterward.
- Inspect an object before mutating a user-named target; treat user-supplied names as hints, not paths. Carry the returned `instanceId` into follow-up calls (`find_method=by_id`) instead of re-resolving by name.
- After editing scripts outside Unity, call `request_recompile`, `wait_for_compilation`, then `get_compilation_errors`. `request_recompile` is rejected in Play Mode - call `exit_play_mode` first. After `enter_play_mode`, poll `get_reload_recovery_status` until ready before the next call (the HTTP server briefly drops during domain reload).
- `get_console_logs` accepts `group_duplicates=true` to collapse spammy repeated logs and `filter_text` to narrow them.
- Large screenshot results automatically fall back to a project-local file. Prefer `save_to_file` when the client can read local files, and use explicit width/height when only a small inline preview is needed.
- Save only the assets you intentionally changed, then read them back to confirm the exact values.

result.instructions:
This server drives the Unity Editor. Core conventions:

- Non-image tool results are JSON envelopes. Success is `{ "success": true, "message": "...", ... }` with an optional payload under `data`; failure is `{ "success": false, "code": "...", ... }`. Branch on `code`, never on human-readable text. Inline screenshots are returned as MCP image content.
- Edit scenes, prefabs, and ScriptableObjects ONLY through these tools / Unity Editor APIs. Never hand-edit .unity/.prefab/.asset files as text while the Editor is open - it overwrites your changes from its in-memory copy.
- To change serialized fields on one prefab component, prefer `set_prefab_property` / `set_prefab_properties`. They avoid Prefab Mode, synchronously reimport the asset, and return persisted readback. Use `open_prefab_stage` only for structural edits; a stage save serializes the full in-memory prefab graph, so review its warning and verify the result afterward.
- Inspect an object before mutating a user-named target; treat user-supplied names as hints, not paths. Carry the returned `instanceId` into follow-up calls (`find_method=by_id`) instead of re-resolving by name.
- After editing scripts outside Unity, call `request_recompile`, `wait_for_compilation`, then `get_compilation_errors`. `request_recompile` is rejected in Play Mode - call `exit_play_mode` first. After `enter_play_mode`, poll `get_reload_recovery_status` until ready before the next call (the HTTP server briefly drops during domain reload).
- `get_console_logs` accepts `group_duplicates=true` to collapse spammy repeated logs and `filter_text` to narrow them.
- Large screenshot results automatically fall back to a project-local file. Prefer `save_to_file` when the client can read local files, and use explicit width/height when only a small inline preview is needed.
- Save only the assets you intentionally changed, then read them back to confirm the exact values.

tools.name: execute_code
tools.description:
[primary] [core] Primary high-flexibility execution tool. Compiles a C# snippet with Unity's Roslyn csc first while preserving the in-memory compilation/execution flow, then runs the compiled assembly on the editor thread. Two templates are supported:
  1) Recommended: implement IFunplayCommand on a class — receives an ExecutionContext (ctx) with RegisterObjectCreation/RegisterObjectModification/DestroyObject (auto-Undo + tracked) and Log/LogWarning/LogError (returned in the response).
  2) Legacy: any class with `public static string Run()` — return value becomes the response message.
Before compiling, the editor's AssetDatabase is refreshed and pending compilation is awaited, so external file edits are picked up automatically without a separate request_recompile (pass skip_refresh=true to bypass this for read-only snippets or a live Play Mode session you must not disturb). When a full-class snippet implements IFunplayCommand, the required Funplay.Editor.Tools.Scripting using is added automatically if omitted. The snippet is compiled into a SEPARATE assembly, so funplay package internal types (e.g. ToolRegistry) cannot be referenced directly from the snippet -- reach them via reflection. safety_checks blocks a small set of obviously dangerous patterns (File.Delete, Process.Start, while(true), Environment.Exit, AssetDatabase.DeleteAsset, etc) and, when strict filesystem safety is enabled, broad System.IO writes plus obvious absolute/system/traversal paths. This is a defensive layer, not a full sandbox. If omitted, the MCP Settings window's default safety-check setting is used (enabled by default); explicitly passing true or false overrides that default. Project namespaces are not auto-injected by default; add `using` directives in the snippet, or enable the ScriptAssemblies-based convenience toggle in the MCP Settings window. If a compile fails with CS0104 (a type name ambiguous between two imported namespaces, e.g. System.Random vs UnityEngine.Random) or CS0433 (a type provided by multiple loaded assemblies) the error carries a structured `ambiguous` list; for CS0104 pass preferred_namespaces (comma-separated) to auto-insert a using-alias binding the name to that namespace and recompile once. CS0433 (same fully-qualified type in two assemblies) can't be fixed by an alias — use extern alias / drop a reference / reflection. Every invocation is appended to a session-scoped history (see get_execute_code_history / replay_execute_code).

code.description: C# code to execute. See description for IFunplayCommand vs legacy Run() templates.

safety_checks.description: If true, reject the call before compile when the code contains obviously dangerous patterns. If omitted, uses the MCP Settings window default.

skip_refresh.description: If true, skip the pre-compile AssetDatabase.Refresh + wait-for-ready. Use only when the editor is already up to date -- e.g. a read-only inspection snippet, or during a live Play Mode session you must not disturb. The default refresh can trigger an import/domain reload (from your own OR another actor's pending changes in a shared editor) that wipes Play Mode runtime state. When skipped, external file edits made since the last compile are NOT picked up.

preferred_namespaces.description: Optional comma-separated namespaces used to auto-resolve CS0104 ambiguity: when an unqualified type name is ambiguous between two imported namespaces, a using-alias binding that name to the candidate in the listed (winning) namespace is inserted and the snippet is recompiled once. Does NOT fix CS0433 (same fully-qualified type in two assemblies). If it stays ambiguous, a structured COMPILATION_FAILED error with an `ambiguous` array is returned.

result.instructions:
This server drives the Unity Editor. Core conventions:

- Non-image tool results are JSON envelopes. Success is `{ "success": true, "message": "...", ... }` with an optional payload under `data`; failure is `{ "success": false, "code": "...", ... }`. Branch on `code`, never on human-readable text. Inline screenshots are returned as MCP image content.
- Edit scenes, prefabs, and ScriptableObjects ONLY through these tools / Unity Editor APIs. Never hand-edit .unity/.prefab/.asset files as text while the Editor is open - it overwrites your changes from its in-memory copy.
- To change serialized fields on one prefab component, prefer `set_prefab_property` / `set_prefab_properties`. They avoid Prefab Mode, synchronously reimport the asset, and return persisted readback. Use `open_prefab_stage` only for structural edits; a stage save serializes the full in-memory prefab graph, so review its warning and verify the result afterward.
- Inspect an object before mutating a user-named target; treat user-supplied names as hints, not paths. Carry the returned `instanceId` into follow-up calls (`find_method=by_id`) instead of re-resolving by name.
- After editing scripts outside Unity, call `request_recompile`, `wait_for_compilation`, then `get_compilation_errors`. `request_recompile` is rejected in Play Mode - call `exit_play_mode` first. After `enter_play_mode`, poll `get_reload_recovery_status` until ready before the next call (the HTTP server briefly drops during domain reload).
- `get_console_logs` accepts `group_duplicates=true` to collapse spammy repeated logs and `filter_text` to narrow them.
- Large screenshot results automatically fall back to a project-local file. Prefer `save_to_file` when the client can read local files, and use explicit width/height when only a small inline preview is needed.
- Save only the assets you intentionally changed, then read them back to confirm the exact values.

tools.name: execute_code
tools.description:
[primary] [core] Primary high-flexibility execution tool. Compiles a C# snippet with Unity's Roslyn csc first while preserving the in-memory compilation/execution flow, then runs the compiled assembly on the editor thread. Two templates are supported:
  1) Recommended: implement IFunplayCommand on a class — receives an ExecutionContext (ctx) with RegisterObjectCreation/RegisterObjectModification/DestroyObject (auto-Undo + tracked) and Log/LogWarning/LogError (returned in the response).
  2) Legacy: any class with `public static string Run()` — return value becomes the response message.
Before compiling, the editor's AssetDatabase is refreshed and pending compilation is awaited, so external file edits are picked up automatically without a separate request_recompile (pass skip_refresh=true to bypass this for read-only snippets or a live Play Mode session you must not disturb). When a full-class snippet implements IFunplayCommand, the required Funplay.Editor.Tools.Scripting using is added automatically if omitted. The snippet is compiled into a SEPARATE assembly, so funplay package internal types (e.g. ToolRegistry) cannot be referenced directly from the snippet -- reach them via reflection. safety_checks blocks a small set of obviously dangerous patterns (File.Delete, Process.Start, while(true), Environment.Exit, AssetDatabase.DeleteAsset, etc) and, when strict filesystem safety is enabled, broad System.IO writes plus obvious absolute/system/traversal paths. This is a defensive layer, not a full sandbox. If omitted, the MCP Settings window's default safety-check setting is used (enabled by default); explicitly passing true or false overrides that default. Project namespaces are not auto-injected by default; add `using` directives in the snippet, or enable the ScriptAssemblies-based convenience toggle in the MCP Settings window. If a compile fails with CS0104 (a type name ambiguous between two imported namespaces, e.g. System.Random vs UnityEngine.Random) or CS0433 (a type provided by multiple loaded assemblies) the error carries a structured `ambiguous` list; for CS0104 pass preferred_namespaces (comma-separated) to auto-insert a using-alias binding the name to that namespace and recompile once. CS0433 (same fully-qualified type in two assemblies) can't be fixed by an alias — use extern alias / drop a reference / reflection. Every invocation is appended to a session-scoped history (see get_execute_code_history / replay_execute_code).

code.description: C# code to execute. See description for IFunplayCommand vs legacy Run() templates.

safety_checks.description: If true, reject the call before compile when the code contains obviously dangerous patterns. If omitted, uses the MCP Settings window default.

skip_refresh.description: If true, skip the pre-compile AssetDatabase.Refresh + wait-for-ready. Use only when the editor is already up to date -- e.g. a read-only inspection snippet, or during a live Play Mode session you must not disturb. The default refresh can trigger an import/domain reload (from your own OR another actor's pending changes in a shared editor) that wipes Play Mode runtime state. When skipped, external file edits made since the last compile are NOT picked up.

preferred_namespaces.description: Optional comma-separated namespaces used to auto-resolve CS0104 ambiguity: when an unqualified type name is ambiguous between two imported namespaces, a using-alias binding that name to the candidate in the listed (winning) namespace is inserted and the snippet is recompiled once. Does NOT fix CS0433 (same fully-qualified type in two assemblies). If it stays ambiguous, a structured COMPILATION_FAILED error with an `ambiguous` array is returned.

tools.description: [core] Diagnose what UI (or physics) elements a click/tap at a screen point would hit, using the live EventSystem's RaycastAll. Returns the full ordered hit chain -- for each hit: hierarchy path, the raycast-receiving Graphic and its raycastTarget flag, sorting info, and the IPointerClickHandler that would actually receive the click (resolved by bubbling up the hierarchy, exactly like uGUI does). The summary names the click receiver, or the element silently swallowing the click when the topmost hit has no click handler anywhere up its parent chain -- the classic 'invisible raycast blocker' bug. Requires a live EventSystem (Play Mode).

Pass `targets` (comma-separated identifiers, or a find spec resolving to at most 100 objects) with a `component` type name to apply the SAME properties to many objects (returns per-target results).

component.description: Component type name (omit if using component_instance_id)

targets.description: Comma-separated identifiers, or a find spec resolving to at most 100 objects (batch; requires `component`)

tools.description: [core] Set a single property or field on a component. Use simple JSON for value (e.g. '5', 'true', '"text"', '[1,2,3]'). Pass `targets` (comma-separated identifiers, or a find spec resolving to at most 100 objects) with a `component` type name to apply the SAME field to many objects (returns per-target results).

target.description: GameObject identifier (omit if using component_instance_id or targets)

tools.name: set_prefab_property

This avoids live Prefab Stage layout/TMP/Spine recomputation, but Unity serialization callbacks can still run. The asset is saved with PrefabUtility, synchronously reimported, and the persisted value is read back. Only serialized fields are accepted; public-member reflection fallback is intentionally disabled. For structural edits such as adding, removing, or reparenting objects, use Prefab Mode.
